slides.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces the 'bias cascade' concept and the REFLEX benchmark, demonstrating that LLM agents often fail to replicate collective social effects despite accurate individual knowledge, a critical challenge for MIMIC's goal of simulating harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLMs align with social knowledge but fail to replicate collective effects due to bias cascades in simulation.
card.key_idea: Introduces REFLEX benchmark to compare knowledge judgment with effect simulation, revealing gaps via Coleman’s boat mechanism.
card.evaluation: Tested 8 LLMs on 30 counterfactual tasks; best model scored 0.847 (knowledge) vs 0.453 (simulation) in net directional scores.
card.limitation: Simulation errors persist even with explicit knowledge injection, indicating fundamental flaws in modeling dynamic human interactions.

slides.title: YYForce Launches Six Seven Humanoid Concierge for Novotel Singapore
slides.highlight: The deployment of a humanoid concierge in a hospitality setting provides a real-world case study for human-robot interaction and social presence, directly relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: NVIDIA Unveils GR00T 2 and Other Robot Technologies at CoRL Conference

slides.title: Crisis Governance at the Joints: Mapping the Ethical and Societal Territory of Crisis Management Technologies
slides.highlight: This paper maps the ethical and societal implications of human-swarm teaming in crisis governance, offering a multi-level framework relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Maps ethical risks in human-swarm crisis tech, arguing problems arise at the joints between interface, infrastructure, and imaginary.
card.key_idea: Proposes a 3i-framework (Interface, Infrastructure, Imaginary) to analyze how ethical issues emerge from translations between these levels.
card.evaluation: Critical literature review across philosophy, AI ethics, and disaster studies; illustrated with two worked examples and design implications.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation or quantitative data, relying solely on theoretical mapping and qualitative case illustrations.

slides.title: Whose Safety? Addressing Anti-Blackness in the Age of AI Safety
slides.tldr: CRITIQUE OF AI SAFETY'S EXCLUSION OF ANTI-BLACKNESS
slides.highlight: This study reveals that AI safety research disproportionately focuses on existential risks while neglecting direct societal harms, particularly anti-Blackness, which is critical for MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: AI safety research ignores anti-Blackness, focusing on existential risks while excluding societal harms affecting Black communities.
card.key_idea: Bibliometric analysis of 69,290 papers (2020–2025) using language models to compare safety and ethics research scope, methods, and racial harm framing.
card.evaluation: Validated via second model, human review, and independent classification; shows safety grew to 6.4% but rarely addresses race or uses human-centered evidence.
card.limitation: Findings depend on abstract-based classification and the specific definition of 'safety' adopted, which may exclude broader sociotechnical harms by design.

slides.title: LanceDB: The data layer for multimodal AI
slides.highlight: LanceDB raised funding to develop a data layer for multimodal AI, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of processing multimodal social perception data.

slides.title: Speaker Attribution and Ideological Congruence in LLM Personas Reading Political Posts
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that LLM personas systematically penalize identical political text based on speaker identity, mirroring human ideological congruence. This is relevant to HyECHO as it provides evidence on how synthetic agents process source cues and social identity signals, informing the modeling of addressee and listener dynamics in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: LLM personas penalize political posts based on speaker identity, mirroring human ideological congruence.
card.key_idea: Fully crossed speaker-attribution experiment using value-grounded personas to measure how leader names alter message evaluation.
card.evaluation: 322k persona-post quartets from X posts; compared against 48 CIS barometers; shows ordinal alignment but not quantitative equivalence.
card.limitation: Single model (gpt-oss-20b) with 2024 knowledge cutoff; personas are synthetic, not real voters; alignment is ordinal only.

slides.title: LanceDB Raises $57.5M Series B to Expand Its Multimodal AI Lakehouse
slides.highlight: LanceDB secured $57.5M in Series B funding to expand its multimodal AI lakehouse, a technology relevant to HyECHO's goal of processing hybrid human-AI team states through non-data-hungry multimodal social perception.

slides.title: WIP: Exploring Student-Created AI Agents and Instructional Videos to Foster Engagement in Computing Education
slides.tldr: STUDENT-CREATED AI AGENTS AND VIDEOS FOR ENGAGEMENT
slides.highlight: This study explores how student-created conversational AI agents and instructional videos foster engagement in computing education, offering insights into human-AI interaction dynamics relevant to modeling engagement in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Students designing AI agents and videos report high engagement and perceived learning in software engineering courses.
card.key_idea: Learners create instructional videos and conversational AI agents using Dialogflow to actively apply and teach course concepts.
card.evaluation: Survey of 19 students (44% participation) using Likert scales and open-ended feedback; high perceived learning scores reported.
card.limitation: Small sample size, lack of control group, and inability to isolate artifact effects from assessment novelty.

slides.title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
slides.highlight: This paper outlines a framework for coordinating multiple large language models to enhance reliability through procedural independence and external verification, relevant to MOSAIC's focus on robust skill acquisition and human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: Proposes a framework for coordinating multiple LLMs in research, emphasizing structured verification over mere model quantity.
card.key_idea: A seven-principle protocol organizing cognitive and verification operations, prioritizing procedural independence and external checks over simple aggregation.
card.evaluation: Illustrated through real-world research cases; lacks quantitative benchmarks or statistical validation of reliability improvements.
card.limitation: Relies heavily on researcher judgment for final decisions, potentially introducing subjective bias despite structured verification steps.

slides.title: The Illusion of Evaluation: Challenges in Agentic Product Evaluation Practice
slides.highlight: This paper highlights the disconnect between agentic model evaluation and real-world product safety, a critical concern for ADAM-CHAT's deployment in dynamic human-AI teaming environments where tool use and context shift.

card.one_liner: Agentic product evaluations often create an illusion of safety by misapplying model-level evidence to complex product risks.
card.key_idea: Identifies six methodological challenges in agentic evaluation and proposes a Transparency and Decision-Relevance Record (TDRR) to link evidence to specific decisions.
card.evaluation: Conceptual synthesis based on practitioner experience and twelve illustrative product contexts; no empirical validation or quantitative results provided.
card.limitation: The TDRR is a reporting aid, not a proof of safety; it risks becoming compliance theater if not paired with valid measurement.

slides.title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding
slides.highlight: This review analyzes how neuro-symbolic grounding and formal logic engines can mitigate hallucinations and invalid reasoning in agentic clinical LLMs, directly informing MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic agent models for trustworthy simulation.

card.one_liner: Proposes a unified framework combining agentic workflows and neuro-symbolic grounding to verify clinical LLM reasoning steps.
card.key_idea: Integrates multi-agent clinical systems with formal symbolic logic engines to enforce verifiable constraints on reasoning trajectories, preventing hallucination cascades.
card.evaluation: Critical narrative review of 98 primary studies (2024-2026) across four paradigms; synthesizes existing evidence rather than conducting new experiments.
card.limitation: The proposed integrated framework remains conceptual and has not yet been validated in real-world clinical settings or against comprehensive benchmarks.

slides.title: Can Cities Have Personalities? Introducing the SCD City Personality Assessment
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a method for generating consistent, evidence-grounded personas for entities using LLMs, which parallels HyECHO's goal of modeling stable social identities and group norms in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: SCD-CPA uses document-grounded AI personas to generate reproducible, comparable city personality profiles.
card.key_idea: City-specific ChatGPT agents grounded in curated documents answer a fixed 24-item MBTI-inspired questionnaire to yield scored urban character profiles.
card.evaluation: Assessed via 33 runs across Tokyo, New York, and Paris, plus 15 runs in five other cities, measuring item agreement and evidence sensitivity.
card.limitation: Scores reflect curated documentary evidence rather than intrinsic city traits, with model interpretation and source selection introducing potential bias.

slides.title: Postpartum Sense-Making and AI in a Fragmented Care System
slides.tldr: LLMs as intermediaries in fragmented postpartum care
slides.highlight: This work examines how LLMs function as intermediaries in fragmented care ecologies, shaping epistemic coordination and responsibility distribution, which informs HyECHO's focus on modeling human-AI team dynamics and social perception in complex interaction settings.

card.one_liner: Argues LLMs in postpartum care must be evaluated for shaping sense-making and care coordination, not just accuracy.
card.key_idea: Positions LLMs as intermediaries in fragmented care, analyzing their impact on epistemic coordination, help-seeking transitions, and responsibility distribution.
card.evaluation: Qualitative synthesis of existing literature on postpartum care gaps, online information ecologies, and current LLM evaluations; no new empirical data.
card.limitation: Lacks empirical validation of how LLMs actually influence user behavior or care outcomes in real-world postpartum settings.

slides.title: Preserving Orientation and Transition Order in Transition Network Analysis: A Directed Topological Proof of Concept
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that directed topological constructions, such as directed flag complexes, preserve transition order and asymmetry in group interaction networks, unlike undirected methods that erase directional structure. This is relevant to HyECHO for accurately modeling the sequential and directional dynamics of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Directed topological methods preserve transition orientation and order in learning analytics, unlike undirected clique baselines.
card.key_idea: Compares Dowker sink/source, directed flag, and GLMY path homology against symmetrized cliques to retain edge orientation and triangle order.
card.evaluation: Tested on group_regulation dataset using null models and bootstraps; directed flag complexes revealed reciprocal loops missed by symmetrization.
card.limitation: Proof-of-concept on a single small dataset (9 states); GLMY path homology yielded trivial results, limiting its utility here.
